precepts.point: You're teaching for who? Teaching our people. Teaching for the Lord. Okay. Where's that at? We're teaching for our people. Yeah. You close, because you teach. Another word for teaching. You going out, and you start with an L. Luke 14. Starts with an L. It has an A. It has an O. Labour. Okay. So you labouring for who? The Lord. Luke 14:23. Oh, you labour for who? You said before. For our people to wake up. Yeah. Okay. Tell me. You know what I'm talking about, sir? Let me hear.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
“He that hath travelled is full of prudence. When I travelled, I saw many things”. Travelling doing what? Teaching. And another word for teaching, when you are going out, starts with an L: labour. That is Luke 14:23, the servant sent out by his lord. You are labouring for the Lord, for our people to wake up.

Sirach says the same of himself: “Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning.” You travel the world and seek out people that want to learn. But first you have to keep the commandments, learn and study, and then go out and teach. Military men travel too; they have been to Syria and Iraq, but they cannot tell you about Dura Europos or the walls of Cyrus. They travel, but they have not studied to know what to look for.

Judith shows why the labour matters: “Now therefore, O brethren, let us shew an example to our brethren, because their hearts depend upon us, and the sanctuary, and the house, and the altar, rest upon us.” The people are depending on us, so it is our job to study, get right, and travel to share the word with our people. Later somebody comes behind you, and you share your experience and teach them. That is part of how you go from milk to meat.

The labour brings experience you cannot get staying home. In Cuba the police came with nightsticks and a paddy wagon; teaching without a license there could bring two years in jail with no trial, and the police chief said this teaching would cause a revolution. Having gone through that, the brethren learned there is a different way to approach it, not to stop teaching there. That is why it is good to get around learned men who have travelled: they understand more than they can express in one conversation.

And the one who labours for the Lord is kept by him: “I was ofttimes in danger of death: yet I was delivered because of these things.” “Whoso feareth the Lord shall not fear nor be afraid; for he is his hope.” If you are sincere in this truth and really keeping his commandments, that spirit will come on you and you will not fear. They said nobody could go up into Laventille in Trinidad because of the gangs; the brethren went up there to teach, and it put a spirit on those men, and now they go up there.

precepts.point: You have to be willing to cut things off at the drop of a dime. This is what the listeners must understand.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.”

That is what Jehoshaphat's princes and Levites did. They “had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.” It is the same pattern we follow, going out into the streets to teach.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

precepts.why:
Christ says from henceforth ye shall catch men. Peter was fishing. “Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.” “Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing”: we’ve been trying to catch these fish all night and we can’t get nothing. “Nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net”: because you said it, Christ, I’ma do it, but we’ve been out all night and didn’t catch nothing.

“They inclosed a great multitude of fishes: and their net brake.” When they threw the net on the other side they had so much fish that the whole net broke. “And they beckoned unto their partners, which were in the other ship, that they should come and help them”: come, get over here quick. “And they came, and filled both the ships, so that they began to sink.”

“When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.” This is Peter showing how humble he was. “For he was astonished”: he was shocked, and all that were with him, at the draught of the fishes; they’re saying, how did he know that? “And so was also James, and John, the sons of Zebedee, which were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.”

That’s what we’re doing when we’re trying to bring our people in: we’re going fishing. There are different kinds of bait you can use, different ways to catch fish. I don’t know how to physically fish, but when we’re out in the street we know how to catch souls; I know how to spiritually fish. Christ used the analogy of fishing for bringing our people into this walk. You have to know how to recruit. You cannot approach everybody the same; everybody is different, but you have to know how to deal with everybody. That’s why Paul said ‘I became all things unto all men, that I might by some means save some.’ That’s what this is about: saving our people.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

precepts.why: One more scripture: “For it is written, I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent.”

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

precepts.why:
“For ye see your calling, brethren”: you have to see your calling. The reason you are in this room is because you are being called. Not everybody is chosen, but your works are going to show if you’re chosen, because if you believe, you’re going to take action. Look what we read about Denmark Vesey: a man has to be so angry, so displeased, that he will take action. So what are you doing to help our people join Israel United in Christ? This is an organization that sets a great example for our people to learn about Christ.

“How that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty”: some brothers that come in are financially well-off, powerful figures, but it’s rare; Paul says not many. “Not many noble”: basketball players. Some of them share the posts, but in their mind they’re thinking, ‘I don’t know if I could join them, I’m going to lose a lot of money, my contracts, my endorsements.’ That’s their trial. Some of them will forsake all, but some are going to follow behind the scenes. Al Sharpton, Louis Farrakhan, Cornel West: how are these figures not here, not chosen? What we could say is maybe in the future. Don’t hold your breath.

“But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise”: the foolish things of the world are us. “And God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty”. “And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen”: you don’t get no lower than a black or Latino. “Yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are”: that’s how the Most High says he’s going to bring this kingdom down.

So it is an honor to be called into this truth, but you’ve got to make your calling and election sure. Part of that is constantly communicating with the brothers, coming to the MOV program, going to the fundraisers: always being involved in the work.

note.label: From Gangbangers To Saviors Of Our Nation

precepts.why: This is the work of making his knowledge manifest in every place. “And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.” We have to go out to the highways and hedges, the corners and the blocks, so his house can be filled.

note.label: | SABBATH EVENING CLASS: Our Salvation & China's Desolation

precepts.why: Christ is saying when you make a dinner or a supper, don’t invite rich people who can pay it back to you. “Call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind”. “Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God”: I don’t know about y’all, but I want to be there. “And they all with one consent began to make excuse”: wicked Israelites that made excuses why they couldn’t repent and follow the Lord. That first group was symbolic of the religious leaders, the scribes, the Pharisees, the Sadducees. “The poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind”: that’s you and me. “Go out into the highways and hedges”: that’s why they went to the northern kingdom of Israel in Acts 13:46; there’s still room, get the rest of them Israelites scattered abroad. “None of those men which were bidden shall taste of my supper”: those scribes, Sadducees and Pharisees will not be allowed to enter in.

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

precepts.why:
“Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” The apostles taught us the same thing Christ did.

This verse gets quoted a lot, but keep it in context. Paul had just been stoned, stoned until the people stoning him thought he was dead; his body must have been horrific. If it wasn’t for the spirit of God he would have been dead, but the disciples gathered round him and prayed and he stood back up. Then he went back to the very same places where he was stoned and told the people, we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.

So there is a spectrum. The end of the spectrum, the extreme and the peak of suffering, is persecution: martyrdom, being put to death, thrown in prison. That is what Paul had just suffered. But in this truth you are going to suffer everything in between, from joyfulness and gladness all the way to persecution, and we must be mentally prepared to face it.

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

precepts.why:
This is speaking of how we are going to obtain immortality and eternal life. “The entrance thereof is narrow”: it is not easy, it is a strict walk, “and is set in a dangerous place to fall, like as if there were a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deep water”. We are walking through perilous times. In these last days the most wicked kingdom on earth is ruling the whole earth, and we have sin and lust all around us and within us. Fire on one side and deep water on the other means there is very little margin for error.

“And one only path between them both, even between the fire and the water, so small that there could but one man go there at once.” That means you can’t save nobody but yourself. You have to endure and fight. You can’t ride into the kingdom on anybody else’s coattail. That’s my officer, that’s my counsel of a thousand: but do you listen to the counsel? Do you apply it? You are not getting the kingdom because you have a righteous counsellor of a thousand. You have to apply yourself.

“If this city now were given unto a man for an inheritance, if he never shall pass the danger set before it, how shall he receive this inheritance?” That danger is the suffering, the pain and the tribulation. “Even so also is Israel’s portion.” That is our portion, our plight.

“Because for their sakes I made the world: and when Adam transgressed my statutes, then was decreed that now is done.” Everything was given to Adam; immortality was given to them. But when Adam transgressed, “Then were the entrances of this world made narrow, full of sorrow and travail”. In this truth there will be sorrow and travail. “They are but few and evil”: few and evil days. Full of perils, which is trouble in all its variations, “and very painful.”

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

precepts.why:
“This is the condition of the battle, which man that is born upon the earth shall fight”. The whole Bible is telling you over and over that you have to fight. It’s narrow; it’s fire on one side and deep water on the other; it’s battle; this is war. It tells you over and over to prepare you mentally for what’s to come. All of us are going to fight.

“That, if he be overcome, he shall suffer as thou hast said”: if you get overcome by the sorrow, by your lust, your temptation, your sin, if you faint in the day of persecution, you are going to suffer as God said. “But if he get the victory, he shall receive the thing that I say.” That is the kingdom.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters”: hate means be willing to cut them off if they are keeping you from God’s law. “Yea, and his own life also”: we all had goals before we heard this gospel, some of them unlawful that would have made lots of money. Some of us are struggling now, and we think if I had taken the other road I wouldn’t be struggling like this. That’s how Satan plays with you.

You being used. You sisters being used. Because guess what? When you hand a flyer, that flyer could change their life, because you bringing them in. That's what we want to be used for, to save lives. Read James 5. What verse do I want? He that converteth the sinner. 20. Come on.

note.label: Final Call: Message to the Black Man

points: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple: you cannot be Christ's disciple if you are not willing to carry your cross, your burdens, and follow after him.

So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple. This is the point of hating mother and father: if you are not willing to forsake all you have, to make sacrifices, including your own life, you cannot be Christ's disciple. You have to be willing to die for what you believe in.

note.label: God, Purpose, and Sacrifice

points: Which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it? You had better sit down and count the cost. People will mock you if you start in this truth and give up: brothers and sisters, you talk all that good talk to your family, and then you go back; they are going to laugh at you. This man began to build, and was not able to finish.

note.label: God, Purpose, and Sacrifice

points: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children: the hate here means you're not trimming your ways against what the Lord said to benefit them. These are persons closest to you, knit to your soul. But if you don't deliver that child up so he can be corrected, because you tried the Bible and it's not working, you're enabling the behavior, and eventually it will pull you out of the truth.

note.label: In a Game of Fools Without The Rules

points: After the video of the apology: once you open your mouth and declare yourself to keep this gospel and teach this understanding, you cannot go back. If any man come to me and hate not his father, mother, wife, children, brethren and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. If you are still tied to family and friends who dishonor the Most High to his face continually, and you want to walk hand in hand with them, the Lord cannot use you. Whosoever doth not bear his cross cannot be my disciple.

Video played: the woke cousin who pulls up to the Fourth of July cookout. A week ago he posted all that Israelite stuff, do not invite me to any Fourth of July or Juneteenth events, do not celebrate birthdays or Easter; now he is at the cookout saying you cannot take Facebook seriously, and eating the pork he called the devil's beef. Captain: this is how you look when you go back on the word of the Lord. Now you are in blasphemy, denying Christ.

When we first started listening to the bishop's classes, we used to ride through the neighborhood with the windows down blasting the class. That joy you once had, you have to renew over and over; you will hit a plateau and have to keep fighting through it. It will come as correction; now you have people saying camp 101 is boring, sitting all day on the Sabbath is boring. This is what we signed up for, because what is lined up for the children of light our minds cannot fathom. Stay on your A game; the gospel is our profession.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: Which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it? He did not count the cost. The same with the entertainer who was shamed on air for endorsing what was done to a child, and you could see his posture drop. He declared, I am an Israelite, the twelve tribes, and then had to say sorry and hold the hand of the one he had exposed. He was not even talking like himself in that clip.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation and is not able to finish, all that behold it begin to mock him: this man began to build and was not able to finish. Some of you take this as a fad and do not count the cost: I am an Israelite this season and next season you are gone; I used to wear those; one time I was an Israelite, I was a Muslim. You played with it. You will be mocked; the Lord purposely sets that spirit so you are exposed: you professed to be a servant of God, and now look at you cutting the cake at the cookout, after all the commanding and hating you did. Shame. Actions shall be weighed.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: Or what king, going to make war, sitteth not down first and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh with twenty thousand? Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage and desireth conditions of peace: he waves the white flag because he did not estimate the overpowering; he was dismayed. That is why the Lord constantly reminds you: be not dismayed by them; do the work; stay focused on the mission, or you will be confounded by the wicked. Stay on the job, harden your face and your spirit constantly.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: When we come into this truth we must prepare ourselves and consider what is to come.
Host: It means you have to deny all the people, even those close or friends, who will drag you back into the world.

He's saying be willing to cut them off, like Matthew 18:8 says the same thing: if thy hand offend thee, cut it off and cast it from thee. Your right hand might be your mother or your father or your wife or your sister, your brother, someone close to you that you love, but those persons are telling you, let's go back to the sins we used to do.
Yea, and his own life also: meaning your own lust within. He cannot be my disciple.
You have to be willing to cut things off at the drop of a dime. This is what the listeners must understand.

note.label: Mistakes We Make in This Truth

points: Does that mean you're supposed to hate your family that may not be in the truth? No. How is that possible when you are supposed to be the light, like it says in Matthew 5:14-16? You're supposed to be an example to them.

It's not talking about you hating them. It's talking about you hating their ways that go against the Lord, especially if those ways are pulling at you to go against the Lord. That's when you have got to observe the time and have discretion: this is not conducive for me, not beneficial in my walk with the Lord. I must remove myself from this situation, from this particular family member that's constantly trying to get me out of the truth.

Oh, here you go reading that Bible again. Or they're always screwing up their face every time you mention or quote a verse. You have got to pay attention to these red flags. That's Satan looking to devour you, and he's using your loved ones to do it.

Are we saying stay away from your loved ones? Absolutely not; you are to be a light and an example to them. But if they are pulling you out of this truth or always coming against you, then you must protect your soul salvation, and sometimes the only way to do that is to be away. Let them see your light shine from a distance, until finally they come: hey, tell me about this, tell me what you're into.

And his own life also: that goes into all the lust and the wickedness in your mindset that you came up in. Most of us in this truth had a whole different lifestyle. All praises to the Lord, we became that new creature in Christ, but we may not have gotten completely rid of that old lifestyle yet.

You have to hate that old lifestyle. If you cannot hate it, the Lord said you cannot be my disciple, because you will infect yourself and the men and women around you. He's coming to make a righteous, purehearted soul. That's who the Lord is looking for.

note.label: Variance It Will Come

points: “Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God.” Now he is going to start the parable. “A certain man made a great supper, and bade many”: a certain man made a big supper and invited many to come.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: “Come; for all things are now ready”: come, for all things are now ready for this dinner.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: “And they all with one consent began to make excuse.” The Pharisees, the scribes, all of them are in here; that’s these religious leaders today, all making excuses for not doing the work. A piece of ground, five yoke of oxen, “I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.” Nobody wants to do the work.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: “Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind”: bring these people to the supper. “And yet there is room”: there is still room left.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: “Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.” Compel our people. Brothers, sisters, that’s our job, and it starts first with the men. Every sanctuary has to be filled, and there’s never enough people, because once we fill up that house we get a new one. This is all a parable of going into the kingdom, but look at it also with these sanctuaries: we are going out and compelling our people to come in.

On the fly mission, giving out flyers, a brother says, ‘Nah, I’m good.’ We don’t accept no, unless you get that one demon that just straight up wants to fight, or some white people that just say no. A lot of our people are saying no just because they’re clueless: ‘Nah brother, I’m good.’ Nah brother, you ain’t good, come back over here. That’s how we have to deal, because whenever we give out these flyers our people are going to say no.

Compel them means we are not giving our people an option: you must come in. This is the truth without a shadow of a doubt; that’s what we’re showing our people. But you have to make your calling and election sure; that’s your job. So why are some brothers still confused? What are you to be confused about? Our people are being oppressed, and the Most High called you to help bring them in. ‘Is God dealing with me? I don’t know’: brother, get the hell out the way. The reason you’re in here is because the Most High called you, so what are you doubting for?

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: “For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?” That tower is your walk with the Lord: whether or not you are going to be able to finish your path to the kingdom. Can you continue in the spirit of Christ keeping the commandments till you die or the sky cracks?

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

points: “Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him, Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.” All of us in this truth are building. We are putting in bricks.

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

points: The king who sits down first and consults “whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand” is counting the cost of war. This truth is war.

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

points: “So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.”

So what is Christ doing with this parable? He is giving us examples of the pain, the struggles and the obstacles we are going to face, to make us mentally prepared before whatever happens, so that we don’t get deceived thinking this truth is a cakewalk. It is not. It is war. That is why our leadership in these last days keeps telling us: stock up, prepare for famine, study, pray, apply, endure, hold the line. There will be things that come against you.

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears
